stories.title: Medieval Strip Farming in England
stories.summary: The medieval practice of strip forming is similar to the "strip cropping" practices carried out in some midwestern states of the USA, except that the origins come from a need to equitably divide land resources around a settlement (strictly managed by the lord of the manor and his officials) rather than having the specific aim of soil conservation and crop management which seems to drive strip cropping in the USA. Medieval strip farming did achieve such aims but it was secondary to the resource allocation issue during the feudal medieval period. In England, the evidence of the strip farming (also called open field farming) having taken place over long periods of time, in the past, is very common. As farmers were allocated long narrow strips of land, in various parts of an open field system (to ensure fair distribution of soil types) the land would be ploughed in such a way that soil would pile up to form a ridge at the centre of a ploughed strip and lower lying furrows at either side...
